It was a pleasure spending time with constituents and learning more about how I can make our state and community even better. This is just the beginning! I look forward to continuing my efforts alongside my colleagues in the Florida Legislature to build on our good work for the people we serve in the next legislative session. If there is something I can do for you, please do not hesitate to get in touch with my office. I want to work with you to build a brighter future for Florida and our district. You can contact my office by. We would be happy to assist you in any way we can! | | Monday, May 20 - Community Foundation of Ocala and Marion County Tour | | Thank you to the board members and staff at the Community Foundation Ocala Marion County for taking the time to show me around the facility. It was great to hear more about the different programs and non-profit partnerships they have going on out in our community. We appreciate everything they do and look forward to working with them in the future to serve the residents of Marion County. | | Tuesday, May 21 - Meetings in Tallahassee | | I had the opportunity to be back in Tallahassee for some important meetings to discuss legislation for the upcoming 2025 Legislative Session. I’m very excited about the next steps we will take to keep our state the Free State of Florida. I look forward to keeping you updated on our progress. | | Wednesday, May 22 - Mental Health Talk at Horse and Hounds Restaurant | | It was great to meet with a group at Horse and Hounds Restaurant to discuss mental health in the state of Florida. I greatly appreciated those who attended the meeting to have important conversations about this topic. In the State House , I will always fight for new and improved resources and additional support for the Floridians facing mental health challenges. | | 2024 Legislative Report Card | | I’m very proud to share with the community that I received 100% on my Florida Chamber Report Card for my work during the 2024 Legislative Session. It was an honor to support pro-business policies in the legislature that will grow and strengthen our state and local economies. Learn more about my score ! | | Memorial Day 2024 | | I hope you enjoyed a meaningful Memorial Day with friends and family. This was a day for us to remember and honor the sacrifices made by the brave men and women in our Armed Forces who laid down their lives to defend our great nation and the freedoms we enjoy here. In the Florida House , I’m committed to being a champion for our active military members and veterans. We owe them so much and should never take their service for granted. | | | Thank you for electing me to serve House District 24 in the Florida Legislature! I’m incredibly honored to be your voice in Tallahassee. As always, if anyone has any questions or concerns, please don’t hesitate to reach out. My office would be happy to help you in any way we can. Have a wonderful week! Best regards, Ryan Chamberlin ****State Representative District 24 | | Copyright © 2024 State Representative Ryan Chamberlin, All rights reserved. | | | Hi team, it's Diana, the Research Director here at the DSCC.

I'm reaching out because polls show President Biden statistically tied with Donald Trump -- but we're _still_ missing your response to our presidential approval poll!

Hey, my team is stressed about reaching our end-of-month fundraising goal, so I’ve been trying to “dial-for-dollars” as much as possible before Friday’s deadline. But between Congressional meetings and votes, time is limited, and I can’t call everyone before the deadline. If you’re all in to help me win, consider chipping in to help us reach our goal right now! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruiz-em-fr-may24?amount=] But if you need more convincing (no worries if you do!) read on...

If we were on the phone right now, though, here’s how our conversation might go:

Hey! Raul here, checking in before my end-of-month Congressional re-election fundraising deadline on Friday to see if you could chip in $. I’m on the ballot again this November, and could really use your support.

There are a lot of members of Congress...remind me, where do you represent?

California! I was raised in a trailer in the Coachella Valley in the District, the son of hardworking farmworkers. After UCLA and Harvard Medical School, I came back home and helped open the first and only low-income clinic for the uninsured and underinsured struggling patients in the area. In 2012, I ran for Congress because our representative was in the pocket of special interests while my patients in the ER and neighbors were in need of a real advocate in Congress. Political insiders said we didn’t have a shot — but I flipped that seat blue. Now, I represent Imperial County, and parts of Riverside County and San Bernardino County, the Southeast corner of California.

OK, that’s a cool story.
But, what have you done in Congress to deserve another term?

I’ve protected Medicare and Social Security, passed laws to modernize Medicaid and expand access to home health services, and introduced legislation to support small businesses, promote humanitarian standards, and help families of fallen public safety officers get back on their feet. Recently, I secured bipartisan support for transitioning the military away from the use of toxic burn pits and resources for our veterans who have been harmed by them.

Who are you running against?

I have a MAGA Republican opponent who wants to ban abortion, touts conspiracy theories about climate change and COVID, and says January 6 was not an insurrection.

For the record, I’m 100% pro-choice, believe in science, and I was there on January 6 when my life was saved by our Capitol Police officers, so I can confidently say it was an insurrection.

Sounds like we need you to win, then.
If I chip in $, what will it be spent on?

Right now, my team needs to buy clipboards for volunteers and order yard signs! We also need to be ready to pay for more expensive items this fall, like TV ads and mailers.

So what do you say? Can I count on you to chip in $ before Friday’s deadline?→ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruiz-em-fr-may24?amount=]

DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruiz-em-fr-may24?amount=]

Thanks for taking the time to talk with me,

Raul

In the summer of 1990, Raul walked in the desert heat from business to business in the Coachella Valley asking them to invest in their community by contributing to his education. With each investment for college, he made a promise to come back home and serve his community as a physician. In 2012, he decided to take his service to the community to the next level by running for Congress. Dr. Ruiz needs our help to continue fighting for us in Congress and to flip the House blue this November.

I also believe that every candidate who asks for your support has a duty to tell you exactly what they stand for and what they’ll fight for. So I’d like to take the opportunity to talk to you about that now, team, if you have a minute to keep reading.
**Unlike the vast majority of elected officials, I know what it’s like to struggle to make ends meet.** I worked all kinds of jobs — at age 12, bagging groceries and waiting tables — to support myself through high school and college. And in Congress, I’m fighting for opportunities for regular people, not special-interest elites.
**Today, I feel like opportunities for hardworking people have been cut in half.** People across our country have been failed by Republican tax policies that have only benefited the wealthiest. We need to change that — while investing in critical areas like childcare, housing, and public education, and strengthening Social Security and Medicare.
**There is no cause greater than American democracy, and I will keep defending it every way I can.** That means defending voting rights here in the U.S. and fighting back against the attacks on our elections coming from MAGA extremists. It means defending democracy abroad by standing up for our allies in Ukraine. And it means getting ahead of the risks of AI and deepfakes to ensure that evolving technology doesn’t imperil the integrity of our elections.
**I have always stood up for abortion rights, and always will.** Here in Colorado, I helped pass one of the nation’s strongest laws protecting abortion rights, and if we flip the House blue this year, we’ll have a great shot at protecting the right to choose in all 50 states. I’m determined to get it done.

# FROM THE DESK OF ALAN DERSHOWITZ
---
| | Dear Peter, In over sixty years in the legal profession, I've experienced first hand the impact of both good journalism and bad journalism — mostly the latter — and just how important and rare it is to get things right.

**In today's media landscape there are far too many publications that get things wrong.** Many are more concerned with the political implications of a story than the basic facts.

**The New York Sun is different.** It's a paper that places principle over politics and people over party.

Its in-depth coverage of the legal challenges faced by President Trump serve as a case in point.

When I defended President Trump during his first impeachment, I faced an avalanche of criticism, but few papers made sufficient effort to fully appreciate the significance of the legal arguments.

The Sun's deeply knowledgeable leadership, including its editor Seth Lipsky and associate editor A.R. Hoffman are themselves students of the Constitution. It shows in their coverage, which I find to be first rate.

It will be no secret to you that I don't agree with everything that can be found in the Sun's pages, but I can say with confidence that its re-emergence is among the most important recent developments in American journalism.

I've been impressed by the Sun's growth so far, but I know it faces an uphill battle, one that I have pledged to join.

**The Sun's success will be a gift to the American people and to the cause of truth.** But to succeed, we need you to join us. I highly encourage you to join the Sun today.

Every person matters in this effort.

Don't wait. The battle to restore American journalism starts now.

Palestinian people during Israel’s 8-month onslaught.

What more needs to happen for Congress and Biden to stop sending bombs and

#
VoteVets does not do anything political on Memorial Day.
Many of us have lost friends and family in service to this nation. Memorial Day is about them. It is a solemn, sacred day.
But Trump...
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-c4-em-may24.RUuZX0&refcode=em240528-1-30&t=1&akid=25735%2E3013755%2Ev0rsOq)

_"Donald Trump is pathetic, childish, and selfish. He doesn't care about those who died in war. He doesn't care about those they left behind. And he doesn't care about anyone other than himself."_
This man calls our fallen “suckers” and “losers” and on Memorial Day, of all days, he showed the clearest evidence yet that their memory means nothing to him.
We cannot allow Trump to regain the title of Commander in Chief. With one term he tore our country apart, and with a second he could destroy the democracy that generations of Americans fought and died for.

| The Republican Party of Texas biennial convention concluded late Saturday afternoon, and #TeamTFVC had an indelible impact from start to finish. In case you weren’t keeping track throughout the last week, Rebecca Hardy and Michelle Evans arrived in San Antonio on Sunday afternoon to prep for committee hearings the following day. Michelle was appointed to the Platform Committee, and sat on two Subcommittees - Health and Human Services and State Affairs - and this responsibility involved 40+ hours of meetings between Monday and Friday to help shape the future of the Republican party. Meanwhile, Rebecca had the opportunity to testify before both the HHS Subcommittee and the Legislative Priorities Committee to get strong language added as a medical liberty plank and as a priority for the 89th legislature to tackle. We are so pleased to say that, thanks to the hard work of delegates leading up to the convention and the presence of TFVC in these important committees,**we succeeded in making vaccine choice a top 15 priority** and ensured that this issue remains prominent on the party platform. But RPT convention wasn’t all business! We had an eye-catching booth manned by hard-working volunteers who helped spread the message of medical liberty to the thousands in attendance. #TeamTFVC got to speak with numerous legislators and conservative influencers about the need for Texas to be a leader in vaccine choice. Plus, Rebecca and Michelle attended the Patriot Gala, where they listened to Congressman Matt Gaetz speak about the tyrannical nature of federal mandates and what the US Congress needs to do to help compensate those who lost their jobs when they refused to comply.
While the work of convention week is over, the work of TFVC continues. **We are so grateful to partner with you in the battle for medical liberty in Texas!**

Looking Ahead
Hello Folks, I hope everyone is ready to kick off the summer! **If you haven’t heard, we have officially suspended our campaign for the state house.** A press release was sent out early last week. That said, we haven’t given up! Far from it. During the summer months, we’ll be “taking a knee” (to use a military term) to catch our breath and decide what is next. I had intended to run for State Senate in 2026, but a few weeks ago, some of you made me rethink that decision. To test the waters I did a poll on Facebook asking our followers where they thought I should run. I expected some state house and state senate answers. I was not expecting the Governor of Minnesota would be the highest vote getter, with the senate coming in last! Right behind running for governor, was state house. While I will not rule out a run for state house in 2026, to work for it now would be disrespectful to Steve. I think we should give him a chance to show us what he can do before challenging him. I don’t want to run just to run either. If I run, it’s because I think I will do a better job of representing you, the people. Let’s give Steve a chance to demonstrate his commitment to us and to Liberty before throwing down the gauntlet! I had not considered running for governor before, but because of your asks, I am starting to think about what that would take. In 2022, I had two complaints about how Scott Jensen ran his campaign. The first was that his campaign seemed to be focused too much on greater Minnesota, which is admirable, however I believe he should've spent more time in the Cities. The second complaint was his selection of Matt Birk as his running mate. I don’t think Matt added much to his ticket. A running mate should be complimentary, someone who will add what you may be missing. I don’t think Birk did that. On that note I did a post last week that upset some because I stated what I would be looking for in a running mate if I decided to run. I would want to name a running mate coming out of the gate so both of us could be campaigning and cover twice as much ground. We would not have big dollars backing us so we need to work harder AND smarter! **I specified three things on my wish list for a running mate:**
1. Someone with credibility and grassroots political experience.
2. Someone who resides near the Cities. I am four hours away and I want someone who understands and is familiar with that area and their issues.
3. I do not want someone who looks like me–another white male. This is what set people off, accusing me of being “woke.” I would argue that people need to wake up to the political facts on the ground. The GOP does have a white male problem. Voters want to see people like them representing them in government. That doesn’t mean race or sex should be the only criteria, or there should be a “token” person in that role, but it does mean that part of a winning strategy is being aware of that and setting yourself up for success–choosing a running mate that expands on your base, not concentrates on it.

We have many conservatives that span the spectrum of gender and race who would add more value to the ticket than another white male. If you can not see this, then you are perhaps part of the problem, and part of what is holding the GOP back. That type of diversity helps to prevent blind spots and issues we may not see because of our culture or heritage. **One last note...** Last week the DFL violated the state Constitution with their last Omnibus bill of the session where they pretty much threw their wish list on the tax omnibus bill 2 hours before the end of the session. This didn’t allow for debate, and it pushed through on a party line vote without a hard copy or electronic copy of the bill in sight. It was around 3,000 pages and covered several topics. This is where the violation of the state Constitution occurred. At the after-session press conference, when asked why they did it, their answer was basically, “We did what we had to in order to pass our agenda.” If I was governor, and a GOP house and Senate did this, I would VETO this bill. Right is right and wrong is wrong, no mater what side is doing it. We either stand on the principles and words of our constitutions or we are no better than the other side who does not. I would love your feedback. I will try to get at least one email out a month throughout the summer months to keep you updated! Thank you all of your continued support. The website will remain active and we are still taking donations to both build the war chest for 2026, and to pay off 2024 debts (we are in the red about $1,500 from this cycle), Any help is appreciated and we do still qualify for the political campaign refund program (yeah, that’s crazy, too).

clean_body: | | | | | | | | May 28, 2024 Looking Ahead Hello Folks, I hope everyone is ready to kick off the summer! If you haven’t heard, we have officially suspended our campaign for the state house. A press release was sent out early last week. That said, we haven’t given up! Far from it. During the summer months, we’ll be “taking a knee” (to use a military term) to catch our breath and decide what is next. I had intended to run for State Senate in 2026, but a few weeks ago, some of you made me rethink that decision. To test the waters I did a poll on Facebook asking our followers where they thought I should run. I expected some state house and state senate answers. I was not expecting the Governor of Minnesota would be the highest vote getter, with the senate coming in last! Right behind running for governor, was state house. While I will not rule out a run for state house in 2026, to work for it now would be disrespectful to Steve. I think we should give him a chance to show us what he can do before challenging him. I don’t want to run just to run either. If I run, it’s because I think I will do a better job of representing you, the people. Let’s give Steve a chance to demonstrate his commitment to us and to Liberty before throwing down the gauntlet! I had not considered running for governor before, but because of your asks, I am starting to think about what that would take. In 2022, I had two complaints about how Scott Jensen ran his campaign. The first was that his campaign seemed to be focused too much on greater Minnesota, which is admirable, however I believe he should've spent more time in the Cities. The second complaint was his selection of Matt Birk as his running mate. I don’t think Matt added much to his ticket. A running mate should be complimentary, someone who will add what you may be missing. I don’t think Birk did that. On that note I did a post last week that upset some because I stated what I would be looking for in a running mate if I decided to run. I would want to name a running mate coming out of the gate so both of us could be campaigning and cover twice as much ground. We would not have big dollars backing us so we need to work harder AND smarter! I specified three things on my wish list for a running mate: 1. Someone with credibility and grassroots political experience. 2. Someone who resides near the Cities. I am four hours away and I want someone who understands and is familiar with that area and their issues. 3. I do not want someone who looks like me–another white male. This is what set people off, accusing me of being “woke.” I would argue that people need to wake up to the political facts on the ground. The GOP does have a white male problem. Voters want to see people like them representing them in government. That doesn’t mean race or sex should be the only criteria, or there should be a “token” person in that role, but it does mean that part of a winning strategy is being aware of that and setting yourself up for success–choosing a running mate that expands on your base, not concentrates on it. We have many conservatives that span the spectrum of gender and race who would add more value to the ticket than another white male. If you can not see this, then you are perhaps part of the problem, and part of what is holding the GOP back. That type of diversity helps to prevent blind spots and issues we may not see because of our culture or heritage. One last note... Last week the DFL violated the state Constitution with their last Omnibus bill of the session where they pretty much threw their wish list on the tax omnibus bill 2 hours before the end of the session. This didn’t allow for debate, and it pushed through on a party line vote without a hard copy or electronic copy of the bill in sight. It was around 3,000 pages and covered several topics. This is where the violation of the state Constitution occurred. At the after-session press conference, when asked why they did it, their answer was basically, “We did what we had to in order to pass our agenda.” If I was governor, and a GOP house and Senate did this, I would VETO this bill. Right is right and wrong is wrong, no mater what side is doing it. We either stand on the principles and words of our constitutions or we are no better than the other side who does not. I would love your feedback. I will try to get at least one email out a month throughout the summer months to keep you updated! Thank you all of your continued support. The website will remain active and we are still taking donations to both build the war chest for 2026, and to pay off 2024 debts (we are in the red about $1,500 from this cycle), Any help is appreciated and we do still qualify for the political campaign refund program (yeah, that’s crazy, too). | | | In Liberty, | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- | Travis "Bull" Johnson for MN House 1B 36167 STATE HIGHWAY 9 SW, BELTRAMI MN 56517 United States You received this email because you signed up on our website or made a purchase from us.

| | China’s intimidation campaign was on full display last week as it [carried](http://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=b90de78796ce4ce596523293a2b8ff82&_m=f6f08128332c4c82b37a4be2a5b83f38&_e=-TB-bLWX8xg3jJJiMn7vMnqUnhd5mA-odG7KAvyt4ucGjAM_XvXZeFfRRMObVyJskpGeqUIdED_aLcq3FGvy8b7WlESNafYabvsALw4a93vMjRFghNy7QjJeNdepr5cigmr3G9tmbVqu9p-EZb0JK6FxCwD-ISyUsK8GaU3qkz4mEkvTIu9Uyn5EI7T3LSAuqArXRR5cz8akcIiriJCGR75kVgBM0iHkTa1CjfUliGU%3D) out large-scale drills around Taiwan. Over two days, Beijing deployed over 100 aircraft and nearly 50 naval vessels encroaching on Taiwan’s ‘contiguous zone’. The reason? ‘Punishment’ for the election of Taiwan’s new president, Lai Ching-te, who Beijing sees as a separatist. Remember, China doesn’t recognize Taiwan’s autonomy, and General Secretary Xi Jinping has made absorbing the island state into China-proper a central focus of the Chinese Communist Party. These drills are not without purpose. Beijing is exercising its military to improve its inter-operability in preparation for a possible invasion, it is trying to intimidate Taiwan, and it is trying to scare Washington into not acting in support of Taipei. We need to stand by Taiwan and against the aggressive rhetoric and actions of the Chinese Communist Party. If we fail to support Taiwan, our entire position in the Indo-Pacific will be undermined.

name: Gene Karpinski, LCV
subject: [ALERT] MAGA Republicans are barrelling towards a vote to overturn historic environmental safeguards >>
body:
__We can 't let this moment pass us by. Pitch in before Friday's end-of-month deadline. |
---

|
Peter, this is flying under the radar because of everything else happening in Congress: _Extreme MAGA Republicans are barrelling towards a vote to overturn historic environmental safeguards._ **We need a MAJOR show of strength to hold the line.**

Here's what you need to know -- Congress could soon vote to:
* _End_ limits on hazardous tailpipe pollution;
* _Force_ a _massive_ build-out of new liquefied methane gas (LNG) export infrastructure; and
* _Gut_ limits on climate- and health-harming pollution from power plants.

**But with only a short window until they vote, we need to act -- _fast_.** Your support will help our campaigns to flood offices with calls and letters, combat misinformation from corporate lobbyists, and keep environmental protections off the chopping block during these legislative fights.

[Please don't wait, Peter. The best thing you can do ahead of our end-of-month deadline is to renew your LCV membership now. Even $5 makes a difference >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)

| | **
** **FOR IMMEDIATE REVIEW**

**Supporter Record:** Peter Willis

**Deadline:** 11:59 pm, May 31, 2024
**Fundraising Goal:** $45,000
**Progress:** 45%

**Peter 's MEMBERSHIP STATUS:** [PENDING -- Renew now >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~) |
---|---|---

We're facing an _absolute onslaught_ of legislative threats from extreme MAGA Republicans as Congress seeks to wrap up business ahead of the busy summer campaign season. That means we're having to fight back on multiple fronts, and it's all happening _right now_.

Here are just a few reasons why your support is so critical in this moment:
* **Congress is gearing up to end limits on tailpipe emissions from vehicles, the number one source of greenhouse gas emissions in the United States.** If we want to stand a chance at curbing climate change, we need to stop the MAGA movement from sabotaging clean, zero-emission cars and trucks. [You can help by renewing your LCV membership for just $5 >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)
* **MAGA Republicans are trying to force through bills to speed a _massive_ build-out of new export infrastructure for liquefied methane gas (LNG).** This greenhouse gas is _80 times more potent_ than carbon dioxide over a 20-year period. We have to stop gas executives from lining their pockets at the expense of frontline communities of color and low income communities. [Please, renew your LCV membership for just $5 >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)
* **Pro-polluter lawmakers are threatening to _eliminate_ limits on toxic air pollution from power plants.** Overturning these safeguards would be disastrous for the health of our communities, our children, and our planet. [Don't wait -- renew your LCV membership for just $5 today >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)__

[We can't let this moment pass us by. Renew your membership before Friday's end-of-month deadline.](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)

Onward,

Gene Karpinski
President

We're tired of having our interests represented in Congress by someone who cares more about what Donald Trump wants than what the people of this district need. It's going to take all of us to fight back against the war chest that John Carter has amassed from D.C. lobbyists and defense contractors, but I know that we're up to the task. You've stood with me every step of the way so far, and I know that you'll be with me from now through November 5. If you can contribute now to help get our campaign headed to victory in November, please do. == | | == | I'm a fifth-generation resident of this district.
